units.text: Begin with carrier-edge placement. Wavelength brings supported compute and storage close to telecommunications users. The goal is a shorter network path for latency-sensitive applications, not a replacement for every regional service.

Move to the VPC extension panel. Enable the Wavelength Zone and create a subnet there. Resources remain tied to their parent Region, so regional dependencies must be included in the application design.

Follow the carrier gateway. Carrier IP addresses and routes enable the intended carrier-network traffic, while security groups and network access control lists still apply. Internet reachability has additional location-specific limits.

With the complete slide visible, validate the actual location. Supported services, capacity, carrier reach and inbound internet support vary by partner and Zone. Test the real user path before choosing Wavelength.

Start with the dedicated connection panel. You receive a dedicated AWS port, but must also arrange carrier delivery and the facility cross-connect. The letter of authorization and connecting facility assignment supports that physical provisioning.

Compare the hosted connection. A Direct Connect Partner supplies a share of its connection, which you accept in your account. Available capacity depends on the partner and location; hosted and dedicated are different provisioning models.

Trace the path on the left from your network to AWS. Assign an owner to the last mile, customer router, facility cross-connect and AWS port. A missing dependency anywhere along this chain can prevent service.

Restore the complete slide and inspect the commissioning checklist. Verify the physical link, VLAN and virtual interface, BGP, and finally application traffic with its return path. A physical link showing up does not prove application access.

Look at the aggregation panel. A link aggregation group uses LACP to combine dedicated connections of the same port speed at one Direct Connect endpoint. Member connections operate active-active, but still share that endpoint.

Check the member limits. A group supports up to four connections at one or ten gigabits per second, or up to two at one hundred or four hundred gigabits per second. All members must use the same speed.

Move to capacity per flow. Traffic is distributed across member connections. Do not assume one flow receives the combined speed of the entire group; size and test the workload's actual traffic pattern.

With the original slide restored, consider the minimum active-link threshold. The group becomes unavailable when operational members fall below that threshold. A LAG does not remove the shared endpoint failure domain; use independent devices and locations for resilience.
